Why every town wants a bigger train station

Marisol Penhallow

Every few years a town council somewhere announces a plan to double the size of its railway station, and every few years the plan quietly shrinks once the costs come in.

This week I want to look at why the ambition keeps coming back, what the bigger stations actually change for the people who use them, and why the answer depends so much on what happens in the streets around them.

Start with the numbers that councils like to quote.
